description: Gating backfill program (80-band). A report of gated coverage — overall and per domain — so a backfill batch's progress is visible and resumable. The start line is the real one: 24 of 245 notebooks gated today. The tracker is computed off the SAME _gated() view-model data the launcher already folds into /api/library's topic rows (gated/locked/passed/checks, from module_gates()), not a second scan, so the number the report shows and the number the app enforces cannot drift. It is surfaced in-app off that same data. This band adds the tracker only; it drives no notebooks (that is 79). Depends on the batched-gating story (79) — the tracker measures what that batch moves. Anti-fabrication: the count is derived from the real presence of a verify_code-passing <slug>.checks.json beside each notebook (the same signal the gate uses), never a stored or asserted number, so it always reflects on-disk reality; a test pins the X/245 arithmetic against a fixture with a known gated subset.
warmup: echo '--- the view-model data to reuse: _gated folds gated/locked/passed/checks into library rows ---'; grep -n 'def _gated\|module_gates\|gated\|checks_path' launcher/app.py praxis/progress.py | head
echo '--- current coverage to reproduce ---'; echo "gated: $(find notebooks -name '*.checks.json' | wc -l) / total: $(find notebooks -name '*.ipynb' | wc -l)"
echo '--- how a library view model already reaches the UI ---'; grep -n 'api/library' launcher/app.py | head

userStories.title: Compute gated coverage overall and per domain
acceptanceCriteria: A coverage report computes gated coverage overall (X/245) and per domain (X/N per domain) off the same _gated()/module_gates() view-model signal the gate already uses — the on-disk presence of a <slug>.checks.json beside each notebook — never a stored or hand-maintained number.
The report reproduces the real starting line (24/245 overall) when run against the shipped library today, so the assertion is grounded in reality rather than a placeholder.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that pins the X/245 arithmetic against a fixture library with a known gated subset (asserting both the overall and a per-domain fraction).

userStories.title: Surface the coverage in-app so a batch's progress is visible
acceptanceCriteria: The coverage report is surfaced in-app off the existing /api/library view-model data (a launcher endpoint or fields folded onto the library response), so backfill progress is visible and a resumed batch's new gates show up without a separate scan.

The UI renders whatever the launcher reports (overall + per-domain fractions) and holds no coverage logic of its own, mirroring how the library badges and KnowledgeChecks render server-supplied state.

Gate green: npm run build in ui/ and cargo build in src-tauri/ pass, python3 -m pytest -q tests/ covers the coverage endpoint, and the progress log shows the coverage number before and after a sample backfill.
